title: Added dissector for The IPv6 Compact Routing Header (CRH)
description: Added a dissector for the IPv6 CRH based on https://tools.ietf.org/html/draft-bonica-6man-comp-rtg-hdr-23.

notes.body: nit: align
Thanks!

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/752/diffs?diff_id=121312092&start_sha=4667e7f34d74cc656e577189b9aad11081d4a147#f4745cb818da81c1b54f17a691313cbd9b28cc5a_275_275)

Yes, will do.

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/752/diffs?diff_id=121312092&start_sha=4667e7f34d74cc656e577189b9aad11081d4a147#f4745cb818da81c1b54f17a691313cbd9b28cc5a_678_678)
Should we have two protocols here? Or rename "ipv6.routing.type.crh".
I think renaming 'ipv6.routing.type.crh' is the preferred option.

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/752/diffs?diff_id=121312092&start_sha=4667e7f34d74cc656e577189b9aad11081d4a147#f4745cb818da81c1b54f17a691313cbd9b28cc5a_3736_3737)
It's not a good idea to break the loop on a PDU value, because we must account for malformed packets.
The loop actually seems to stop by chance on a padding field. Or am I misunderstanding?

You're right. The correct stopping condition should be `offset < rt->hdr.ip6r_len + 32 && sid`, I believe.

This assumes `ip6r_len` is not malformed, however. Is there something else that could be done?

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/752/diffs?diff_id=121312092&start_sha=4667e7f34d74cc656e577189b9aad11081d4a147#f4745cb818da81c1b54f17a691313cbd9b28cc5a_1228_1229)

Trusting `ip6r_len` is fine, it's hard to see how we could do better than that... TVBs will safely catch out of bounds errors.

What is the meaning of `rt->hdr.ip6r_len + 32`? Sorry, I don't follow the logic here.

Good question. In 4.3 of https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc8200, we see `Hdr Ext Len` provides us with the length of the header in 8-octet units, not including the first 8 octets. 4 of those first 8 octets are for (Next Header  |  Hdr Ext Len  | Routing Type  | Segments Left) fields.

That means the number of octets of SID's = Hdr Ext Len + 4 octets.
Although, now that I think of it, I think that would imply the stopping condition would be `offset < rt->hdr.ip6r_len + 4`... I think `32` was a mistake on my part.

Would this work?

```
if (is_crh16)
    sid_count = rt->hdr.ip6r_len * 4 + 2
else
    sid_count = rt->hdr.ip6r_len * 2 + 1
    
for (unsigned i = 0; i < sid_count && sid != 0; i++) {...}
```

It's consistent with the other routing dissectors that loop over address count but using byte offsets would be fine too.
Much cleaner. Thank you.
Done!

It's great that you provided a test capture, thanks for that, but it needn't and shouldn't be added to the repo tree (unless there is a test case and this doesn't fit the scope). Not sure where the file should be placed after the migration to GitLab. Anyone?
Please add the URL to the draft, including of course the revision number.
Will do.

After giving it a little more thought I'm inclined to think using FT_NONE here is somewhat flawed. We should have FT_UINT16 and FT_UINT32 for CRH-16 and CRH-32 respectively.

That could be achieved with separate protocols or just different header fields.
